description: _amip-noirr_ is one experiment under the framework of IRRMIP historical simulations (also including _amip-irr_, _hist-irr_, _hist-noirr_), whose objective is to assess the impacts of historical irrigation on climate, energy balance, water balance, and carbon cycle. By comparing the _amip-_ and _hist-_ experiments, we can also explore the role of the ocean in the spread of irrigation-induced impacts. The first phase of IRRMIP is described in [Yao et al. (2025a)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-56356-1)  and [Yao et al. (2025b)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s44221-025-00529-1). The protocol of _amip_noirr_ requires the modelers to run the simulations with amip mode (with atmosphere and land components active) for the historical period with transient greenhouse gas emissions/concentrations and land-use, etc, **with the irrigation deactivated**. If limited by resources, a 30-year simulation representing the present-day climate and human activities is also welcome, but please keep it consistent with _amip-irr_, _hist-irr_, _hist-noirr_.
